title: Genitive 2: Feminine Endings (-ы and -и)
description: Feminine nouns ending in -а take -ы in the genitive (-и after к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, ч). Feminine nouns ending in -я take -и.
descriptionRussian: Женские существительные на -а получают окончание -ы (или -и после к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, ч). Существительные на -я получают окончание -и.
intro: Feminine nouns bring back a spelling rule you have now met in three different books: once deciding noun plurals, once deciding adjective endings, and now here. If it is still costing you thought, this is the lesson to finally fix it, because it is not going to stop appearing. Everything else today is a single swap at the end of the word. The rule sitting on top of it is the only place a mistake is likely.
rules: Feminine nouns ending in -а swap -а for -ы in the genitive: комната → комнаты, газета → газеты, сестра → сестры.
Feminine nouns ending in -я swap -я for -и: неделя → недели, песня → песни, кухня → кухни.
Spelling rule: write -и instead of -ы after к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, ч. So книга → книги (not 'книгы'), кошка → кошки. The grammar is the same; only the letter changes.
examples: У меня нет комнаты. (I don't have a room.) комната → комнаты.
На столе нет газеты. (There is no newspaper on the table.) газета → газеты.
У Лены нет книги. (Lena doesn't have a book.) книга → книги (spelling rule).
В квартире нет кухни. (There's no kitchen in the apartment.) кухня → кухни.
У Антона нет машины. (Anton doesn't have a car.) машина → машины.

tables.title: Feminine Genitive: -а → -ы (or -и after к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, ч)

items.hint: Feminine -а changes to which letter in the genitive?
items.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in -а swap -а for -ы in the genitive: комната → комнаты. The construction 'у Х нет ___' triggers genitive, just like in Lesson 1.

items.promptEnglish: There is no newspaper on the table.
items.explanation: The pattern is consistent: -а replaces with -ы. Газета → газеты, just like комната → комнаты.

items.hint: Beware the spelling rule. Russian can't write -ы after к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, ч.
items.explanation: Книга would become 'книгы' by the regular rule, but Russian's spelling rule says: after к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, ч you must write -и instead of -ы. So книга → книги. The same rule will apply to other words whose stem ends in к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, or ч.

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 1: what ending did masculine consonants take?
items.explanation: Quick recap from Lesson 1: masculine nouns ending in a hard consonant add -а in the genitive. Журнал → журнала. Today's lesson is feminine, but this masculine pattern stays warm in your memory.

items.hint: Soft -я swaps to which soft vowel?
items.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in -я take -и in the genitive. Тётя → тёти. The soft -я always swaps to soft -и.

items.hint: Кошка ends in -ка. Which letter must follow к?
items.explanation: Кошка ends in -ка, so the spelling rule applies: write -и not -ы. Кошки. Even though кошка is animate (a cat), genitive does not care about animacy. Both animate and inanimate feminine nouns follow the same pattern after к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, ч.

blanks: У меня нет _____. (I don't have a sister.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Сестра is feminine ending in -а. Genitive: -а → -ы → сестры.

errorCorrection.sentence: У Антона нет машина в гараже.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton doesn't have a car in the garage.
errorCorrection.explanation: After нет the noun shifts into the genitive. Машина is feminine ending in -а, so the genitive swaps -а → -ы: машины. The -ы ending is the standard feminine genitive after most consonants.

errorCorrection.sentence: У нас нет ручка на столе.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: We don't have a pen on the table.
errorCorrection.explanation: After нет, ручка shifts into the genitive. Normally -а swaps to -ы, but the spelling rule blocks -ы after к, г, х, ж, ш, щ, ч. Ручка's stem ends in -к, so the ending becomes -и instead: ручки.

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня нет кухня в новой квартире.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I don't have a kitchen in my new apartment.
errorCorrection.explanation: After нет the noun shifts to the genitive. Кухня is feminine ending in -я (the soft counterpart of -а); the soft-stem feminine genitive ends in -и: кухни. The -я → -и pattern is the soft parallel of -а → -ы.

minimalPairs.explanation: After есть ('there is X' / 'one has X') the noun stays in the nominative: комната. The genitive form комнаты appears in the opposite construction: 'У Маши нет комнаты' (Masha doesn't have a room). Есть keeps nominative, нет triggers genitive.
After нет the noun shifts into the genitive. The regular rule would give -ы (книгы), but the spelling rule converts that to -и after к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, ч. So книга → книги.

reviewVocab.example: Книга, школа, мама — это женский род.
Окончание -а меняется на -ы или -и в родительном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: whom? (the genitive question word for people and animals)
reviewVocab.example: У кого нет книги? — У Антона.
